scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic actor can consume a check result after another actor advances the guarded shared-state generation because no authoritative revalidation edge binds check to use.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled inert consumer records the checked generation and the generation actually consumed, without mutating production data or causing an external side effect.
scenarios.positive_control: With no interfering generation change, the same actor pair reaches the inert consumer exactly once and the checked generation equals the consumed generation.
scenarios.negative_control: With mandatory generation revalidation enabled, advancing the shared-state generation between check and use is rejected before the inert final consumer commits.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the harness cannot keep both actors inside the synthetic owned fixture, if timing escapes deterministic barriers, or if any uncontrolled external state would be affected.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Replay the exact deterministic interleaving after adding generation revalidation and require stale use to be rejected while the same-generation positive control still succeeds.
scenarios.shared_invariant_state_generation: The guarded decision is valid only for logical shared state fixture account-A at generation 41; actor B advances that same logical state to generation 42 before actor A uses the decision.
scenarios.actor_operation_generations: Actor A is synthetic-checker operation generation A-7; actor B is synthetic-mutator operation generation B-3; their identities and attempt generations remain fixed across control and test.
scenarios.scheduler_executor_identity: Both actors run on controlled executor fixture exec-check-use-v1 with a test barrier that deterministically suspends actor A after the check observation and before the use operation.
scenarios.synchronization_happens_before: The intended contract requires state mutation generation 42 to happen-before a fresh authorization/state revalidation, but the failing schedule permits use to follow the old check without that edge.
scenarios.check_use_commit_trace: Actor A checks generation 41, barrier releases actor B to publish generation 42, actor A resumes without revalidation, and the inert consumer receives the decision derived from generation 41.
scenarios.queue_publication_state: No queue ordering is assumed; barrier state and generation-tagged publication are explicit, and the shared fixture records the authoritative generation transition before actor A resumes.
scenarios.cancellation_retry_teardown_state: Cancellation, retry, and teardown are disabled in this case and their fixture generations remain constant, preventing lifecycle changes from explaining the stale decision consumption.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: The final consumer is inert-decision-sink/check-use-v1, which only records actor identity, check generation, consumed generation, and whether the stale decision was accepted.
scenarios.effective_concurrent_capability: The only exercised concurrent capability is permission to submit one inert marker based on a previously checked state generation; no production privilege or external authority is involved.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one synthetic receipt showing checked_generation=41, consumed_generation=42, and accepted=true under the controlled bad interleaving.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Receipt CR-CU-001 is emitted only by the inert final consumer after it validates the exact fixture, actor operation generations, and state-generation tuple for this run.
scenarios.counterfactual_schedule: Hold actors and state constant but add the generation revalidation edge before use; the same barrier schedule must then reject the stale decision while preserving the positive path.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject stale logs, different logical state instances, barrier mis-ordering, independent policy changes, and marker emission before mutation by correlating fixture and receipt generations.
scenarios.evidence_level: CR3 is appropriate if the inert final consumer accepts the stale checked generation under the deterministic schedule with all controls passing.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Evidence is capped at CR3 until a bounded reversible effect, complete counterfactual schedule set, eliminated alternatives, and remediation regression support CR4 or CR5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Two synthetic completion actors can both observe a pre-commit state and commit the same logical operation because the single-effect transition is not serialized or generation-guarded.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled fake ledger acts as an inert single-effect sink and records only synthetic commit markers for one owned operation generation, without invoking real payments, jobs, or external actions.
scenarios.positive_control: When completions are serialized through the intended single-effect guard, exactly one synthetic ledger entry is recorded and the neighboring successful completion behavior remains intact.
scenarios.negative_control: When one completion has already advanced the operation generation, the second completion is rejected by the corrected guard and produces no second inert ledger entry.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort if either completion path can reach a real external action, if the fake ledger is not the only consumer, or if the deterministic barrier cannot isolate the intended commit race.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Replay both completion actors at the same controlled barrier after adding an atomic single-effect transition and require exactly one ledger entry with no loss of valid completion behavior.
scenarios.shared_invariant_state_generation: Logical operation fixture op-77 may transition from pending generation 9 to committed generation 10 exactly once; two entries for the same operation generation violate the single-effect invariant.
scenarios.actor_operation_generations: Actor A is completion callback comp-A generation 4 and actor B is retry completion comp-B generation 2; both target the same logical operation fixture op-77 generation 9.
scenarios.scheduler_executor_identity: Both completion actors execute on mock executor exec-complete-v2 and are released from a deterministic pre-commit barrier only after each has observed the pending state.
scenarios.synchronization_happens_before: The required contract needs one completion commit to happen-before the other actor's state revalidation, but the failing schedule allows both actors to pass the pre-commit observation concurrently.
scenarios.check_use_commit_trace: Each actor reads pending generation 9, both reach the barrier, then both attempt the commit point; the fake ledger records whether one or two commit markers are accepted.
scenarios.queue_publication_state: Completion dispatch order is treated as unspecified; only the deterministic barrier and operation-generation transition define the experiment, so enqueue order cannot be mistaken for execution order.
scenarios.cancellation_retry_teardown_state: The second actor is a synthetic retry generation and no cancellation or teardown occurs, allowing the test to isolate duplicate completion from lifecycle invalidation effects.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: The final consumer is fake-ledger/single-effect-v2, which accepts only inert synthetic markers and tags every entry with operation generation and completion actor identity.
scenarios.effective_concurrent_capability: The effective capability is limited to appending one synthetic marker for the owned operation fixture; no external transaction, privilege, or irreversible side effect is permitted.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a deterministic ledger count and two actor-tagged entries if the invariant fails, or exactly one entry when the single-effect guard works correctly.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Receipt CR-DC-001 binds ledger state to operation op-77, generation 9, both completion actor generations, barrier epoch, and the final single-effect consumer.
scenarios.counterfactual_schedule: Keep both completion actors and the same pending generation but enable the atomic commit-generation transition; one actor must win and the second must observe committed state and stop.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject duplicate harness injection, stale ledger contents, distinct operation IDs, idempotent-by-contract behavior, and pre-barrier marker emission through generation-tagged ledger receipts.
scenarios.evidence_level: CR4 is supportable when the controlled schedule causes two bounded inert commits for one operation generation and the result is tied to the exact actor/interleaving tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Evidence remains below CR5 until remediation replay, alternative-explanation elimination, and the full synchronization/receipt provenance demonstrate regression-verified causal proof.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic work item can commit after cancellation advances the lifecycle epoch because completion does not revalidate the current cancellation or teardown generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A read-only controlled sink records whether a synthetic work item generation is accepted after cancellation acknowledgement, using only owned fixture epochs and inert result markers.
scenarios.positive_control: Without cancellation, the same work-item generation commits one inert result through the controlled sink and produces the expected current-epoch receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: After cancellation acknowledgement with epoch revalidation enabled, the same stale work-item generation is rejected before the final sink accepts any result marker.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if cancellation cannot be acknowledged deterministically, if the work item can touch a real service or persistent queue, or if teardown would affect anything outside the owned fixture.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Replay the exact cancellation/completion ordering after adding epoch revalidation and require stale completion rejection while a non-cancelled current-epoch work item still succeeds.
scenarios.shared_invariant_state_generation: Synthetic task fixture task-12 may commit only while lifecycle epoch 5 is active; cancellation advances the authoritative epoch to 6 and revokes completion authority from work generation 5.
scenarios.actor_operation_generations: Actor A is worker work-12 generation 5 and actor B is canceller cancel-12 generation 6; both identities and lifecycle epochs are explicitly recorded in the fixture.
scenarios.scheduler_executor_identity: Worker and canceller run on mock executor exec-cancel-v1 with barriers around cancellation acknowledgement and final commit, making the stale-completion schedule deterministic.
scenarios.synchronization_happens_before: The intended ordering requires cancellation acknowledgement epoch 6 to happen-before worker commit revalidation, but the failing path allows worker generation 5 to commit without checking epoch 6.
scenarios.check_use_commit_trace: Worker observes active epoch 5, canceller advances and acknowledges epoch 6, worker resumes at commit without revalidation, and the read-only sink records whether stale work was accepted.
scenarios.queue_publication_state: The synthetic work item remains in a mock queue whose dispatch order is not used as evidence; lifecycle epoch and acknowledgement receipts are the authoritative ordering signals.
scenarios.cancellation_retry_teardown_state: Cancellation request and acknowledgement are generation-tagged; no retry occurs, teardown remains synthetic, and the worker carries the stale pre-cancellation operation generation.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: The final consumer is read-only cancellation sink cancel-sink-v1, which records task generation, current lifecycle epoch, cancellation acknowledgement, and acceptance state.
scenarios.effective_concurrent_capability: The only effective capability is submitting one inert completion marker to the owned read-only sink; no external job, resource mutation, or privilege-bearing action is reachable.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured synthetic receipt showing stale work generation 5 accepted after authoritative cancellation epoch 6, or rejected after remediation.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Receipt CR-CC-001 is keyed by task fixture, worker generation, cancellation generation, acknowledgement epoch, executor identity, and final consumer identity.
scenarios.counterfactual_schedule: Keep task, worker, canceller, and epochs fixed but insert mandatory lifecycle-epoch revalidation immediately before commit; stale generation 5 must then be rejected.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject late-but-permitted completion semantics, stale acknowledgement logs, different task instances, queue reorder assumptions, and marker emission before cancellation by checking exact receipt generations.
scenarios.evidence_level: CR3 applies when the read-only final consumer accepts stale work after acknowledged cancellation under the deterministic controlled schedule.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Evidence is capped at CR3 until a bounded reversible state effect and full remediation regression establish the stronger CR4 or CR5 causal chain.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic reader can consume a published object generation before initialization is complete because publication lacks the required ordering or visibility edge.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled read-only consumer inspects a synthetic structured object containing generation-tagged initialization markers and never dereferences production pointers or mutates external state.
scenarios.positive_control: When initialization completes before publication with the intended barrier, the read-only consumer observes all required fields for the current object generation.
scenarios.negative_control: When the corrected publication fence is active, the consumer cannot observe the object until all generation-tagged initialization fields are complete and visible.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort if the fixture cannot guarantee synthetic object ownership, if publication reaches a production registry, or if reproducing the schedule requires unsafe memory corruption or uncontrolled load.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Replay the same publisher/reader schedule after adding the required publication ordering and require complete initialization to be visible while normal publication behavior remains successful.
scenarios.shared_invariant_state_generation: Synthetic object fixture obj-P generation 18 is consumable only after fields header, policy, and payload all carry initialization generation 18 and publication generation 18.
scenarios.actor_operation_generations: Actor A is publisher pub-P operation generation 8 and actor B is reader read-P operation generation 11; both target the same logical object generation 18.
scenarios.scheduler_executor_identity: Publisher and reader execute under controlled executor exec-publish-v1 with barriers that can expose publication after header initialization but before policy and payload initialization.
scenarios.synchronization_happens_before: The correct contract requires all initialization writes for generation 18 to happen-before publication and reader acquisition; the failing schedule omits that full ordering edge.
scenarios.check_use_commit_trace: Publisher initializes header, publishes the reference, reader acquires and consumes, then publisher finishes remaining fields; the read-only consumer records which generation-tagged fields were visible.
scenarios.queue_publication_state: Publication state is explicit and generation-tagged; no queue FIFO assumption is used, and reader acquisition is released only by the controlled publication barrier.
scenarios.cancellation_retry_teardown_state: Cancellation, retry, and teardown remain disabled with constant generations, isolating initialization/publication ordering from lifecycle or duplicate-attempt effects.
scenarios.final_consumer_identity: The final consumer is read-only-structure-sink/pub-v1, which reports field completeness and generation tags without mutating the object or invoking any privileged behavior.
scenarios.effective_concurrent_capability: The exercised capability is only to read the owned synthetic object after publication; no write outside the fixture, external request, or privilege-bearing operation is possible.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured read-only marker showing publication generation 18 with one or more initialization fields missing or carrying the wrong generation.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Receipt CR-PI-001 binds the object generation, publisher and reader operation generations, publication barrier epoch, visible field generations, and final consumer identity.
scenarios.counterfactual_schedule: Hold object and actors constant but enforce initialize-before-publish with the required fence; the same reader acquisition must then observe a complete generation-18 object.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject stale object reuse, reader targeting a different generation, fixture default values, logging reorder, and post-consumption mutation by verifying immutable generation-tagged receipt fields.
scenarios.evidence_level: CR3 is appropriate when the read-only consumer deterministically accepts a partially initialized current object generation under the controlled publication schedule.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Evidence cannot exceed CR3 without a bounded reversible effect or stronger result plus full counterfactual, alternative-explanation, receipt, and remediation evidence.
